title: Why Mario has a moustache
hook: Mario's moustache, cap and overalls were all workarounds for tiny pixels.
peek: Mario's look is one of the most recognised in the world. It was designed in 1981 for a character only 16 pixels across, and almost every feature solved a drawing problem rather than expressing a style.
lede: When Shigeru Miyamoto designed the hero of Donkey Kong in 1981, he had a sprite of about 16 by 16 pixels and very few colours. A mouth would not show up at that size, so he gave the character a big moustache. Hair was hard to draw and animate, so he added a cap. The famous look came from the hardware.

bullets.text: In the arcade game the character was known as Jumpman, a carpenter climbing girders to rescue a woman from a giant ape. He only became Mario, and a plumber, in later games.
Miyamoto chose overalls in a contrasting colour so players could see the arms swing as the character ran. With so few pixels, a plain shirt would have blurred into the body.

bullets.opening: A big nose for a face
bullets.text: The large nose also did a job: together with the moustache, it made the face readable as a face. A tiny cluster of pixels became a cheerful, recognisable person.
The name came from Nintendo of America's staff. The usual story is that their warehouse landlord, Mario Segale, interrupted a meeting about late rent, and they named the hero after him.
